sentences.text: ?Neutral Citation No. - 2025
Court No. - 36
Case :- First Appeal Defective No. - 447 of 2023

Appellant :- Roopchand And 8 Others
Respondent :- National Highway Authority Of India And 10 Others
Counsel for Appellant :- Rahul Kumar Tyagi Counsel for Respondent :- Manoj Kumar Yadav,Raj Kumar Yadav,Satya Prakash Hon'ble Kshitij Shailendra,J.

1. Heard Shri Rahul Kumar Tyagi, learned counsel for the appellants and Shri Satya Prakash,
learned counsel for private respondents.
2. The matter is being listed for deciding the question of deficiency of court fees as reported by the Reporting Section.

On the earlier occasion, the matter was referred to Taxing Officer of this Court,
who has passed an order dated 01.04.2024 making the appellants liable to pay deficient court fees of Rs. 3,45,590/-.
3. The appellants were granted time to file objections against the said order and address the Court against the order of Taxing Officer.

4. Shri Rahul Kumar Tyagi, learned counsel for the appellants submits that the Taxing Officer has invoked Section 8 of the Court Fees Act and has held the appellants liable to pay ad valorem court Roopchand And 8 Others vs National Highway Authority Of India And ... on 7 January, 2025 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/46584561/
1 fees treating the matter as if the appellants are claiming enhancement of compensation determined by the Additional District Magistrate (Acquisition)/Competent Authority, Ghaziabad, whereas it is the case where in terms of the provisions of Section 3(H) of the National Highways Act, 1956,
entitlement to receive compensation amongst private parties was sought and, hence, Section 8 of the Court Fees Act has no application.

5. Per contra, Shri Satya Prakash submits that appellants themselves filed a reference case under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894 read with National Highways Act as is apparent from page No. 111 of the paper book and, therefore, the determination shall be deemed to be under Section 18 and since the appellants have themselves invoked appellate jurisdiction of this Court under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act, the appellants are liable to pay court fees.
6. Having heard learned counsel for the parties and having carefully examined the record, I find that there was a dispute of entitlement to receive compensation determined by the Additional District Magistrate (Acquisition)/ Competent Authority, Ghaziabad and, therefore, the application was moved before the District Judge.

The District Judge while considering the application, titled under Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, observed that the matter was referred under Section 3H(4)
of the National Highways Act, 1956.

The determination made by the order impugned dated 19.10.2023 is in the nature of adjudication under Section 3 H(4) of the Act whereby the claim of the appellants has been rejected and the private respondents have been held entitled to receive compensation.

7. Merely because the application moved before the District Judge mentioned Section 18 of the Land Acquisition Act, the same in itself does not make the application maintainable under the said provision and the Court has to see the facts of the case, prayer made in the application and also determination made under the order impugned.
8.

In view of the facts and circumstances and the record of proceedings, this Court finds that the instant appeal under Section 54 of the Land Acquisition Act is not maintainable and for this reason,
the appellants are not required to deposit any court fees.
9.
The instant appeal is, accordingly, dismissed as not maintainable with liberty to the appellants to institute appropriate proceedings.

10. The impugned order dated 19.10.2023 shall be treated as simplicitor order under Section 3H(4)
of National Highways Act, 1956 and not under Land Acquisition Act, 1894.
11. Office is directed to return certified copies attached to the appeal to the learned counsel for the appellants within one week after retaining photostat copies thereof on record.
